Persons owned as property within Scythian society; ownership is a relational material fact independent of legal standing.
Biological/socially assigned females; the category is independent of the rights system.
Adult free males of native Boiotian parentage; while the label is political, the criteria are biological and genealogical.
Persons having undergone formal education (paideia); this is a social/attainment fact, not a legal definition.
Individuals performing specific ritual/devotional roles for the cult of Cronus/Saturn; defined by vocational activity.
Adult males not owned as property; the status of 'free' is the absence of a property relation, not the presence of a legal right.
Adult free males of local descent; criteria are genealogical and biological.
Persons possessing significant material assets or high income; wealth is a material economic position.
Biological/socially assigned females; age and ancestry are unspecified but female sex is the defining criterion.
Persons owned by another; the ownership relation is a relational fact existing prior to specific legal regulations.
Individuals defined as the property of a Dominus; ownership is the constitutive fact.
Biological/socially assigned females; the label identifies sex independent of Republican legal standing.
Persons in the early developmental life stage; age is a biological/social developmental fact.
Persons engaged in the study or teaching of philosophy; defined by vocational/intellectual activity.
Free residents of non-Aeginetan ancestry; criteria are residence and genealogy.
Adult males without offspring; the group is defined by the biological/relational fact of being childless.
Individuals performing temple duties/rituals; defined by vocational/sacral role.
Adult free local males physically capable of combat; criteria are sex, age, ancestry, and physical capacity.
Defined by productive and protective vocational roles in Late Period Egypt; generally free males of modest to middle material standing.
Identified by developmental life-stage (advanced age) and sex; biological facts independent of legal status.
A person acting in a non-official/private capacity. While contrasted with magistrates, the underlying human is an adult free native male.
Adult free male of local ancestry; criteria are genealogical and biological, common to Greek poleis in Cyprus.
Offspring born of parents in a recognized union; kinship and biological descent are law-presupposing but rights-independent.
Defined by active participation in political assembly and speech; requires rights of speech (isēgoria) and status to participate.
Possession of significant material resources/surplus; a fact of economic capacity rather than a specific legal grant.
Free native males of the respective Greek member-states; ancestry and sex are the independent identifiers.
Relational fact of physical control and use of land or capital; presupposes a concept of property but is an economic relation.
Relational fact of exercising ownership over another person; constitutive of the master-slave economic relationship.
Specifically those exercising the right to sue or being sued in court; defined by the procedural legal action itself.
Foreign ancestry population brought under control through military conquest; identified by origin and physical location.
Persons appointed by a specific legal decree to represent the state; role is entirely created by legal/diplomatic commission.
Office-holders whose identity is defined by the holding of a legal title/authority granted by the polity.
Individuals of native ancestry physically located outside the territory due to compulsion/proscription.
Material ownership and management of maritime vessels; an economic and vocational role independent of legal status.
Vocation involving the wholesale trade of goods; economic role identifiable by activity regardless of citizenship.
Physical absence from the territory of the polity; a spatial-geographical fact.
The subset of native free males with the highest material wealth/yield; economic standing within the native group.
Holders of state leases for mines; the category is defined by the legal contract/concession from the state.
Adult male defined by biological relation (son) to a specific female kin (widowed mother); criteria are kinship and life-stage.
Adult biological males within the population; sex and age are the primary filters.
Vocationally identified by labor on ships; frequently associated with the thetes (lower wealth) but defined by occupation.
Legal liturgy performed by highest wealth class; role is defined by legal obligation to maintain a ship.
An official role assigned to men in their 60th year; defined by legal-administrative function.
Free status combined with foreign ancestry and local residence; independent of specific rights.
A composite group defined by non-native ancestry and/or property status (slavery).
Genealogical fact: male biological offspring in a lineage.
Biological descendants of a specific ancestor regardless of sex.
Offspring where maternal ancestry is non-native; genealogical fact prior to rights status.
State-owned enslaved persons of Scythian origin serving as public order workers.
Members of the native ancestry cohort with high material-economic yields.
Persons of Scythian ethnic/geographical origin regardless of legal status.
Specifically defined by participation in the court system; eligibility is rights-based (adult male citizens).
Vocational role in religious/cultic service; often hereditary or selected from native families.
Defined solely by advanced age/life-stage.
Free native-born residents of Attica; used as an ethnic/political designation independent of specific voting rights.
Free native males with low material wealth and physical impairment; criteria are biological/economic.
Persons owned as property; includes those enslaved for debt in the Solonic context (prior to abolition).
Minor children whose fathers are deceased; defined by age and kinship status.
Biological females of the native population; categorized by sex and residence independently of their lack of political standing.
Referred to by vocational role; generic placeholder for persons performing specific labor or crafts.
Defined by holding a public office; membership is contingent on the legal selection system (sortition or election).
Persons performing ritual/sacrificial duties; while often state-sanctioned, the vocational/ritual role is a distinct behavioral fact.
Adult free male of native lineage in Oreus; ancestry and sex define the cell even if laws regarding their rights vary.
Citizens of the constituent poleis of the League; defined by native ancestry in their respective member cities.
Adult free males of Delphic ancestry; a sub-population defined by geography and lineage.
Children of native men killed in military service; defined by age and kinship (deceased father) rather than legal status.
A person seeking physical protection at a sacred site; defined by the act of supplication and physical location.
Body of 500 citizens; membership is strictly defined by legal selection and political office-holding.
Combined group of non-native ancestry, including both those owned as property and free foreign residents.
Individuals accused of killing a person; the state of being a suspect is a fact of accusation, not a defined right or office.
Persons who have caused death without intent; defined by the physical act and psychological state.
Spartan Spartiates with high material standing (ability to contribute to syssitia); defined by wealth and ancestry.
Persons captured in war and held under coercion; their status is a relational fact of capture and ownership.
Same as Athens: individuals seeking religious asylum at a temple, regardless of social status.
Defined by male sex and kinship descent from a native male (citizen); biological/genealogical fact.
Persons possessing physical health/fitness; a biological/medical status.
Professional teachers of wisdom/rhetoric; categorized by their vocational activity.
Individuals possessing significant land or capital; based on material productive capacity.
Free adult male native citizens who specialize in public speaking; 'legal' role is professional/vocal rather than an office.
Persons experiencing physical or mental infirmity; a biological state independent of legal standing.
Those with significant material resources, social influence, or persuasive capacity (pisteis) in the community.
Vocational role defined by the performance of music or poetry; spans citizens, metics, and slaves.
Religious officials whose status is often tied to specific cultic laws and lineage/office-holding requirements.
Legislators (nomothetai) are a specific functional office of the state; poets are a vocational role.
Biological and developmental stage; free male offspring of native residents.
High material wealth and social prestige (e.g. liturgy-payers); observable by lifestyle and economic capacity.
Biological/socially-assigned male sex and adult life-stage.
Biological/socially-assigned female sex and adult life-stage.
Men of high-status lineage and high wealth; ancestry and economic status are observable independent of specific rights.
Vocational role defined by the practice of medicine; can be citizens, metics, or free foreigners.
Professional performer of epic poetry; vocational role independent of legal status.
High-wealth native-born individuals currently residing outside the polity's territory due to expulsion.
Adult males not owned as property; includes citizens, metics, and free foreigners.
Developmental life-stage of individuals in Macedonia; non-adult age.
Individuals owned as property by others; the relational fact of ownership is the primary identifier.
Free residents of Syracuse with foreign genealogical ancestry.
Free foreign adult males whose primary productive role is providing military service for pay.
Athenian ancestry is the rigid-designator fact (descent from Attic citizens) and is independent of the polity hosting the rule; relative-to-polity status is captured separately by rule_polity.
Persons of native ancestry physically removed or living outside the territory of the polity; the physical location and genealogical link are rights-independent.
Free persons living in the territory who do not descend from the local citizen lineage; defined by residence and ancestry.
Inhabitants of the city of Delphi; a geographical and ancestral designation regardless of their status within the Roman imperial legal framework.
Free adult males of local Attic ancestry; during the Roman period, this identifies the local municipal elite and eligible residents.
Defined by the lack of formal Greek education (paideia), a cultural-intellectual attribute independent of legal standing.
The ethnikon of persons originating from or residing in Tarsus; a fact of geographic origin and ancestry.
A combination of biological age (elderly), sex (male), and the relational fact of having offspring (fathers).
Defined by their ritual/vocational role; however, in Rome, high priesthoods are offices within the state apparatus, making them rights-mediated.
Individuals with high material-economic resources, whether derived from land, trade, or capital.
Defined solely by biological life-stage; the advanced age of the individual.
A vocational role involving the transmission of knowledge and literacy for compensation or within a school context.
Female musicians/entertainers, often associated with low social standing but defined by their specific occupational performance.
Foreigners who received local citizenship via a legal act; the status is intrinsically rights-defined despite the foreign ancestry.
Persons not belonging to the specific community or kinship group; defined by lack of local ancestry or connection.
Adult males who are not legally owned as property by another person; the status is the negation of slavery.
Young individuals engaged in formal learning under an instructor; defined by life-stage and activity.
Defined by productive role; skilled manual laborers or craftsmen.
Males within the age range of physical maturity (roughly 18-60) capable of manual/martial activity.
Individuals who live at the table of the wealthy in exchange for social services/flattery; defined by economic dependency and lack of profession.
Defined by vocational performance in theatre and music; a socially distinct group regardless of legal infamia.
Professional performers in the Roman theater; often of low social status or enslaved/freed, identified by their vocational role in public entertainment.
Individuals engaged in dance for entertainment or ritual; a vocational role generally associated with the infamia category in Roman social hierarchy.
Males of distinguished lineage and material wealth; 'high-born' refers to genealogical facts and ancestral prominence within the local Greek city-state context.
Individuals who have undergone specific ritual transformations in a cult (e.g. Mithraic, Isiac); participation is a social/religious fact independent of civil law.
Persons physically located outside the territory of the polity; defined strictly by the geographic fact of non-presence.
Individuals specializing in creative or mimetic production (sculptors, painters, etc.); defined by their specific vocational output.
Males serving in organized military units; defined by their vocational role in the state's armed forces.
Individuals holding delegated authority within the imperial bureaucracy; the role is defined by legal appointment to an office.
Professional teachers of rhetoric and public speakers; defined by their vocational prowess and educational role.
Free persons residing in Athens who lack native Attic ancestry; defined by genealogical origin.
Citizens who actively practice public speaking and political leadership; defined by their behavior/activity in the Assembly.
Males in a marital relation; defined by the social/kinship fact of being a partner in a household union.
Persons not owned by another; the status is the inverse of the ownership relation.
Individuals with high material assets or agricultural yields (e.g. 500-bushel men and knights); defined by economic capacity.
Restricted group of native males defined by the oligarchic coup's legal limit (the 400); selection is rights-dependent.
The 5,000 citizens in the 411 BCE regime, defined by their ability to provide hoplite equipment; defined by a legal threshold for inclusion.
Magistrates overseeing grain supply; office-holders whose role is defined by legal mandate and appointment.
Individuals of high economic standing; identified by material surplus and productive capacity independent of rights.
Minors born to enslaved parents; their status as property is inherited genealogically/relationally.
Individuals identified by their adherence to Christian religious practice and community membership; a social/ideological fact.
Persons of low material-economic position and social standing, often those without land or significant movable wealth.
Minors whose fathers are deceased; identified by biological life-stage and kinship absence (lack of pater familias).
Individuals in the early developmental life-stage (infants/children/youth) within the community.
Biological/socially-assigned females within the early Christian community across all ages and social statuses.
Persons in a pre-adult developmental life-stage, regardless of sex or social status.
Persons whose primary role is manual or productive vocational labor, typically of lower economic status.
Males of the Tribe of Levi by patrilineal descent; ancestry is a genealogical fact independent of cultic rights/duties.
The supreme religious office-holder; eligibility is tied to Aaronic descent, but the role itself is an office defined by the cultic system.
Males of Aaronic descent; the category is genealogical (native ancestry) and linked to vocational service.
Elder leaders within the community; selection is rights-mediated through religious appointment/standing, though often linked to age.
Defined by deviation from community doctrine; the category is intrinsically defined by the ideological/legal norms of the group.
